post-cm02-force-superposition.physical_scope: Adoption of the framework's force branch: force maps as continuous, state-locally-Lipschitz vector-valued maps on a time window, an open configuration domain and velocity space, the equation of motion $m_i\ddot x_i=F_i(t,x,\dot x)$ in every inertial frame, pointwise additivity of declared force contributions, and the transformation rule that a force law must satisfy under a change of inertial frame. The postulate excludes impacts, dry and static friction, stochastic and distributional forcing, and constraint reactions; it asserts no measured value, no conservation law and no claim that any physical interaction is exactly of this form.

post-cm02-force-superposition:
## Postulate

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about
forces and motion, in the spacetime, frames and worldlines of
[[post-cm01-spacetime]], [[post-cm01-frames]] and [[post-cm01-worldlines]].

**(i) Setting and configuration domain.** A model of the framework has
$N\ge1$ particle labels with fixed positive masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}$
([[post-cm01-worldlines]], clause (v)) and a configuration domain $Q$ in one
fixed inertial frame, in the unconstrained branch of
[[def-cm01-configuration]] clause (a): $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ is open,
possibly with the collision set $\Delta$ removed when the force law of the
model is singular at coincident positions. The constrained branch of that
definition, with its reaction forces, is **not** covered by this postulate; the
dynamics of constrained systems is a separate development with its own
assumptions. A **state** of the model is a pair $z=(x,v)\in Q\times\mathbb
R^{3N}$ of positions and coordinate velocities of the labels in the chosen
frame ([[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]]).

**(ii) Time window.** A model carries a nondegenerate open interval
$I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$, its **time window**, read in seconds
([[def-cm01-units]]).

**(iii) Force map and standing regularity.** A **force map** on this data is a
map

$$F:I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}\longrightarrow(\mathbb R^{3})^{N},\qquad (t,x,v)\longmapsto F(t,x,v)=\bigl(F_{1}(t,x,v),\dots,F_{N}(t,x,v)\bigr),$$

with components of dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$, read in newtons
([[def-cm01-units]]). The standing hypotheses of this branch, which every
force map of a model is required to satisfy, are:

1. **Continuity.** $F$ is continuous on its domain
   $D:=I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$.
2. **State-local Lipschitz regularity, locally uniform in time.** $F$ is
   locally Lipschitz in the state variable $z=(x,v)$, locally uniformly in
   time, in the sense of [[def-locally-lipschitz-in-the-state-variable]]: every
   compact cylinder $C\subseteq D$ carries a finite $L\ge0$ with
   $\lVert F(t,z)-F(t,z')\rVert_{2}\le L\lVert z-z'\rVert_{2}$ whenever
   $(t,z),(t,z')\in C$ share their time coordinate.

A map that fails clause 1 or clause 2 is **not** a force map of this branch,
whatever its other merits. When a later statement differentiates the force map
(for instance in a linearization or a smooth-dependence claim), it adds the
required differentiability hypothesis of the state variable explicitly; clause
2 alone licenses only the existence, uniqueness and continuation statements
proved on this page.

**(iv) Equation of motion.** Adopt: the motion of the labels of a model with
force map $F$ in an inertial frame is governed by

$$m_{i}\,\ddot x_{i}(t)=F_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),\dot x(t)\bigr)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N),$$

imposed along families of $C^{2}$ coordinate curves of the labels
$x=(x_{1},\dots,x_{N}):J\to Q$, where $J\subseteq I_{0}$ is an interval with
nonempty interior and the derivatives are those of
[[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]]. The precise notion of a motion of the
model, its associated first-order system and its maximal motions is
[[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]. The force map is **primitive data** of the model:
the equations above are the model's law, not an operational definition of $F$
from a measured acceleration, and $F$ is not an extra observable measured
independently of the motion. The mass $m_{i}$ in (iv) is the fixed inertial
mass of clause (v) of [[post-cm01-worldlines]]; no other mass occurs in this
clause.

**(v) Additive composition of force contributions.** When a model presents its
force map as composed of contributions, the composition is the pointwise sum:
for force maps $F^{(1)},\dots,F^{(k)}$ on a common domain satisfying (iii),

$$F(t,z)=\sum_{a=1}^{k}F^{(a)}(t,z),$$

and the sum again satisfies (iii), because a finite sum of continuous maps is
continuous and a finite sum of maps that are locally Lipschitz in the state
variable is locally Lipschitz with a locally uniform constant. This
**superposition of forces** is an adopted modelling rule, not a theorem about
nature: it says how the model's total force is composed from the contributions
it declares. Two decompositions with the same sum define the same force map
and the same model; the framework does not measure an individual contribution
in isolation, and no observation of motions alone determines a decomposition.
Nor does (v) assert that sums of motions are motions: if $F$ is not affine in
the state, the sum of two solutions of (iv) generally does not satisfy (iv),
and superposing solutions is a separate question from superposing forces.

**(vi) Description in another inertial frame.** Let $F_{*}=\bigl(o',u',
(e_{1}',e_{2}',e_{3}')\bigr)$ be a second inertial frame related to the frame
of (i) by the Galilean transformation

$$t'=t+b,\qquad x'=Rx+vt+a_{0}$$

with $b\in\mathbb R$, $a_{0},v\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and $R\in SO(3)$
([[pthm-cm01-galilean-kinematics]] clause 1;
[[def-cm-special-orthogonal-group]]). If $x:J\to Q$ is a family of motions of
the labels in the first frame and $\eta(t'):=R\,x(t'-b)+v\,(t'-b)+a_{0}$ is
the description of the same worldlines in the second frame, then by clause 2
of that theorem $\eta$ is of class $C^{2}$ on $J+b$ and
$\eta_{i}''(t')=R\,\ddot x_{i}(t'-b)$, so along the motion (iv) becomes

$$m_{i}\,\eta_{i}''(t')=\bigl(R\,F\bigl(t'-b,\ x(t'-b),\ \dot x(t'-b)\bigr)\bigr)_{i}.$$

Adopt: the same interaction, read in the second frame, is represented on the
transferred data by the map

$$F_{*}(t',y,w):=R\,F\Bigl(t'-b,\ R^{\mathsf T}\bigl(y-v(t'-b)-a_{0}\bigr),\ R^{\mathsf T}(w-v)\Bigr),$$

whose domain is the image of $D$ under the affine bijection
$(t',y,w)\mapsto\bigl(t'-b,\,R^{\mathsf T}(y-v(t'-b)-a_{0}),\,R^{\mathsf T}(w-v)\bigr)$;
that domain is open, and $F_{*}$ is continuous and locally Lipschitz in its
state variable because $F$ is and the transfer is an affine bijection with
bounded inverse on compacta. The framework formulates the equation of motion
in every inertial frame; a rule that does not transform by this law is a
description tied to the frame in which it was written, and the framework
attaches no kinematic covariance to it. When $Q=\mathbb R^{3N}$ — the case of
the models of the companion page — the transferred domain is again a product
$I_{0}'\times\mathbb R^{3N}\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ with $I_{0}'=I_{0}+b$, and
$F_{*}$ is a force map in the sense of (iii); for a bounded $Q$ the
transferred admissible position set may depend on $t'$, and the equation is
then read on that transferred set.

**(vii) What this branch excludes.** Impulsive forcing (a finite momentum
transfer at an instant is not a force map); Coulomb sliding friction, whose
expression contains the factor $v/\lvert v\rvert$ and is undefined at $v=0$;
static friction, which requires an inequality or a set-valued reaction model;
stochastic forcing; and forces that exist only as distributions. Each of these
requires its own stated model and solution notion, and none is covered by
(iii)–(iv). A singular force law is admissible on a configuration domain with
the singular configurations removed — for instance an inverse-square law on
the collision-excluded $Q$ of clause (i) — and what the removal of those
configurations implies for existence in time is stated by the continuation
theorem of this page.

**(viii) Status.** Clause (iii) states the hypotheses under which the theorems
of this page are proved; clause (iv) is the adopted law of motion; clauses (v)
and (vi) are the adopted composition and frame rules. Nothing here is deduced
from experiment, from a symmetry principle or from the uniqueness theory of
differential equations, and nothing here asserts that any physical
interaction is exactly of this form: the theorems of this page are conditional
consequences of the adopted model. The empirical significance of a concrete
model lies in fully specified model parameters and reported observations
compared with its predictions, and this postulate supplies neither.

post-cm02-interactions.physical_scope: Adoption of restricted interaction models inside the force branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: a decomposition of the total force into external single-label forces and pair forces, the optional pair assumptions of antisymmetry and centrality, the branch of force maps that come from a scalar potential with the Euclidean gradient, and the optional Newtonian gravitational pair-potential model with gravitational coupling parameters distinct from the inertial masses. The item asserts no law of nature, no measured value and no conservation law; the identification of gravitational and inertial mass is recorded as a further empirical assumption, not adopted.

post-cm02-interactions:
## Postulate

Adopt, whenever a model of the force branch [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]
invokes them, the following **restricted interaction assumptions**. Throughout,
the data $I_{0}$, $Q$, $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}$ and the force map $F$ are those of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], and a state writes $z=(x,v)$ with
$x=(x_{1},\dots,x_{N})\in Q$ and $v=(v_{1},\dots,v_{N})\in\mathbb R^{3N}$.

**(i) External-plus-pair decomposition.** The model's force map is presented as

$$F_{i}(t,z)=F_{i}^{\mathrm{ext}}(t,x_{i},v_{i})+\sum_{j\ne i}F_{ij}(t,x_{i},x_{j},v_{i},v_{j}) \qquad(i=1,\dots,N),$$

where each $F_{i}^{\mathrm{ext}}$ is a single-label **external** force map and
each $F_{ij}$ (for $i\ne j$, an ordered pair) is a **pair** force map, all
defined on their stated open domains and satisfying the standing continuity
and state-local-Lipschitz hypotheses of clause (iii) of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with respect to the arguments they actually
depend on. This is a restriction of the model class: an arbitrary force map
$F$ of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] need not admit such a decomposition,
and the decomposition is part of the model's declaration, not a theorem. It is
relative to the declared set of labels: for a subsystem, a pair force to a
label outside the declared set appears as an external force, and no
antisymmetry or pairing property of the full system restricts that external
force.

**(ii) Optional pair assumptions.** In addition, a model may adopt, separately
or together, the following assumptions about a pair force $F_{ij}$:

1. **Antisymmetry (strong form of the third law).**
   $F_{ij}(t,x_{i},x_{j},v_{i},v_{j})=-F_{ji}(t,x_{j},x_{i},v_{j},v_{i})$ for
   all arguments in the domain.
2. **Centrality.** $F_{ij}(t,x_{i},x_{j},v_{i},v_{j})$ is parallel to
   $x_{i}-x_{j}$, i.e. lies in the real line spanned by $x_{i}-x_{j}$,
   whenever $x_{i}\ne x_{j}$.

Each assumption is a further restriction of the model class and is adopted
only where invoked. Both are *sufficient* hypotheses used by later balance
statements, and neither is a consequence of the equation of motion: a
velocity-dependent pair force, or an interaction mediated by a field omitted
from the declared labels, need satisfy neither.

**(iii) Potential model.** A model may present its force map through a scalar
**potential** $U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), of dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$, read in joules ([[def-cm01-units]]), through the rule

$$F_{i}(t,z)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N),$$

the gradient being the Euclidean gradient in the position variable of each
label ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]],
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). This is a restriction of the force class:
only force maps that are the negative gradient of such a potential belong to
it. The same force map arises from every potential of the form
$U(t,x)+c(t)$ with a differentiable function $c$ of $t$ alone whenever
the declared $C^{2}$ regularity is retained. More generally, for each connected
component $C$ of $Q$ (a maximal connected subset), two $C^{2}$ potentials
for the same force differ by an independently chosen $C^{2}$ function
$c_C(t)$ on $I_0\times C$. A single time function suffices when $Q$ is
connected; openness alone does not require the constants on different
components to agree. The chosen normalization is part of any later energy
statement and is recorded with it, and no energy statement is made on this page.

**(iv) Pair and external potentials are examples, not the general form.**
When $U$ has the form

$$U(t,x)=\sum_{i}u_{i}(t,x_{i})+\sum_{i<j}u_{ij}(t,x_{i},x_{j})$$

with $C^{2}$ scalar functions $u_{i}$, $u_{ij}$, the decomposition (i) holds
with $F_{i}^{\mathrm{ext}}=-\nabla_{x_{i}}u_{i}$ and
$F_{ij}=-\nabla_{x_{i}}u_{ij}$. Potentials of the still more special form
$u_{ij}=u_{ij}(t,\lvert x_{i}-x_{j}\rvert)$ are the **central pair
potentials**; these are examples, and no generality is claimed for any of
these subclasses. Velocity-dependent forces such as the drag model
[[post-cm02-drag]] lie outside every potential model of this clause.

**(v) Newtonian gravitational branch.** The model may adopt the pair potential

$$U_{ij}(x_{i},x_{j})=-\frac{G_{\mathrm N}\,m_{i}^{g}m_{j}^{g}}{\lvert x_{i}-x_{j}\rvert}$$

on the collision-excluded configuration domain ($x_{i}\ne x_{j}$ for all
$i\ne j$), where $G_{\mathrm N}>0$ is a constant of dimension
$\ell^{3}\mu^{-1}\tau^{-2}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]) and the numbers
$m_{1}^{g},\dots,m_{N}^{g}>0$ are **gravitational coupling parameters** of the
labels, primitive model data distinct from the inertial masses $m_{i}$ of the
equation of motion. By clause (iii) this potential supplies the attractive
inverse-square pair force
$F_{ij}=-G_{\mathrm N}m_{i}^{g}m_{j}^{g}\,(x_{i}-x_{j})/\lvert x_{i}-x_{j}\rvert^{3}$,
the content of the elementary differentiation
$\nabla_{x}\bigl(1/\lvert x-y\rvert\bigr)=-(x-y)/\lvert x-y\rvert^{3}$; a
concrete instance of that differentiation is verified on the companion page.
The adopted model satisfies the antisymmetry and centrality options of (ii)
where they are invoked.

**(vi) The mass identification is an empirical assumption.** The
identification

$$m_{i}^{g}=m_{i}\qquad(i=1,\dots,N)$$

of gravitational couplings with inertial masses is **not** part of clauses
(i)–(v) and is not a consequence of the equation of motion. It is an
additional empirical assumption, adopted only when a model states it, and it
is the subject of the weak equivalence principle; the sources record its
empirical support and its historical status, and this page records no
measurement. Likewise, the inverse-square form in (v) is an adopted law, not a
consequence of the force branch [[post-cm02-force-superposition]].

**(vii) Status.** Clauses (i)–(v) are adopted modelling assumptions that
restrict the force maps of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]; they add no
dynamics beyond that postulate, and every theorem of this page remains
conditional on these adopted hypotheses. The balances of momentum, angular
momentum and energy, when asserted later, are theorems with their own
hypotheses on this structure and are not made here.

def-cm02-newtonian-flow.physical_scope: Vocabulary of the force branch: the state space of positions and velocities, the inverse-mass operator, the associated first-order system of the second-order equation of motion, motions as its solutions, initial data, the maximal motion and its maximal interval, and the Newtonian flow map. The item defines objects only; it asserts no force law beyond the cited postulate, no regularity of the flow beyond what the cited existence theorems provide, and no empirical claim.

def-cm02-newtonian-flow:
## Definition

Let a force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] be given: time window
$I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$ nondegenerate and open, configuration domain
$Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ open ([[def-cm01-configuration]] clause (a)),
fixed masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), and a
force map $F$ with the standing continuity and state-local-Lipschitz
hypotheses of clause (iii) of that postulate.

**(a) State domain and inverse-mass operator.** The **state domain** of the
model is

$$D:=I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3N}\times\mathbb R^{3N},$$

an open subset of $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{6N}$; a point $(t,x,v)\in D$ is a
time together with the **state** $z=(x,v)$ of positions $x\in Q$ and coordinate
velocities $v\in(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$ of the labels ([[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]],
[[def-cm01-units]]). The **inverse-mass operator** is the linear map

$$\mathsf M^{-1}:\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad \mathsf M^{-1}(u_{1},\dots,u_{N}):=\Bigl(\frac{u_{1}}{m_{1}},\dots,\frac{u_{N}}{m_{N}}\Bigr),$$

the inverse of the mass operator $\mathsf M$ of clause (d) of
[[def-cm01-configuration]].

**(b) Associated first-order system.** The **associated first-order field** of
the model is

$$\mathcal F:D\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{3N}\times\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad \mathcal F(t,x,v):=\Bigl(v,\ \mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,v)\Bigr),$$

and the **associated first-order system** is $z'=\mathcal F(t,z)$ on the open
domain $D$, in the sense of
[[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]; here
$z=(x,v)\in\mathbb R^{6N}$. The map $\mathcal F$ satisfies the
Picard–Lindelöf hypotheses of
[[thm-picard-lindelof-local-existence-and-uniqueness]]: it is continuous on
$D$, and it is locally Lipschitz in the state variable $z$ locally uniformly
in time, because its first component $z\mapsto v$ is linear and its second is
the composition of the force map $F$ — which is locally Lipschitz in $(x,v)$
locally uniformly in time by [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause (iii) —
with the linear map $\mathsf M^{-1}$.

**(c) Motions.** Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
interior, endpoints read with one-sided derivatives as in
[[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]. A **motion** of
the model on $J$ is a curve $x:J\to Q$ of class $C^{2}$ such that
$t\in I_{0}$ for every $t\in J$ and

$$m_{i}\,\ddot x_{i}(t)=F_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),\dot x(t)\bigr)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N,\ t\in J).$$

Equivalently: the state curve $z=(x,\dot x):J\to D$ is a solution of the
associated first-order system on $J$. Indeed, if $x$ is a motion then
$z=(x,x')$ is $C^{1}$ with
$z'=(x',x'')=(x',\mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,x'))=\mathcal F(t,z)$ and $z(t)\in D$;
conversely, if $z=(x,v)$ is a solution with $z(t)\in D$ for all $t$, then
$x'=v$ and $v'=\mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,v)$, so $v$ is $C^{1}$, $x$ is $C^{2}$, and
multiplying the second equation by the masses returns the displayed
second-order equation. Motions of the labels of the model are exactly these
curves by [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause (iv).

**(d) Initial data and maximal motion.** An **initial datum** of the model is
a triple $(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})$ with $t_{0}\in I_{0}$, $x_{0}\in Q$ and
$v_{0}\in(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$; write $z_{0}:=(x_{0},v_{0})$. A **maximal
motion** with this datum is a motion $x:J_{\max}\to Q$ with $x(t_{0})=x_{0}$
and $\dot x(t_{0})=v_{0}$ that has no extension to a motion of the model on a
strictly larger interval. By the Picard–Lindelöf hypotheses verified in (b)
and the maximal-solution theorem
[[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-a-maximal-ode-solution]] (with
[[def-maximal-ode-solution]]): every initial datum has exactly one maximal
motion, its **maximal interval** $J_{\max}$ is an open interval containing
$t_{0}$ and contained in $I_{0}$, and every motion with the same datum is the
restriction of the maximal one. The restriction statement transfers from the
associated first-order system to motions through the equivalence in (c).

**(e) Newtonian flow.** The **Newtonian flow** of the model is the map

$$\Phi:\Omega\longrightarrow Q\times\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad \Omega:=\bigl\{(t,t_{0},z_{0}):t_{0}\in I_{0},\ z_{0}\in Q\times\mathbb R^{3N},\ t\in J_{\max}(t_{0},z_{0})\bigr\},$$

defined by $\Phi(t;t_{0},z_{0}):=z(t)$, where $t\mapsto z(t)=(x(t),\dot x(t))$
is the state curve of the maximal motion with datum $(t_{0},z_{0})$. By (d) the
assignment is well defined: the maximal motion is unique, so $\Phi$ is a
function on $\Omega$ and not merely a relation. For fixed $t_{0}$ and $z_{0}$
the curve $t\mapsto\Phi(t;t_{0},z_{0})$ is defined exactly on the maximal
interval $J_{\max}(t_{0},z_{0})$.

pthm-cm02-ivp.physical_scope: The local existence, uniqueness and maximal-extension statement for the adopted Newtonian force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] on an open configuration domain: every initial datum with a configuration in the domain and an arbitrary coordinate velocity admits a unique motion through it, locally in time, and there is a unique maximal motion of which every motion with that datum is a restriction. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted force postulate and the cited mathematical ODE theorems; it gives no global existence, no bound on the interval, no empirical statement and no claim that any physical system realizes the model.

pthm-cm02-ivp:
## Statement

Adopt the force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: time window
$I_{0}$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$, masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, and a force map $F$ continuous and locally Lipschitz in
the state variable, locally uniformly in time, on
$D=I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$. Let
$\mathcal F(t,x,v)=\bigl(v,\mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,v)\bigr)$ be the associated
first-order field and let motions and maximal motions be as in
[[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]. Fix an initial datum
$(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})\in I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$ and write
$z_{0}=(x_{0},v_{0})$.

1. **Local existence.** There is $h>0$ and there is a motion $x$ of the model
   on $[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]$ with $x(t_{0})=x_{0}$ and $\dot x(t_{0})=v_{0}$;
   moreover such a motion is exactly one of class $C^{2}$ satisfying
   $m_{i}\ddot x_{i}(t)=F_{i}(t,x(t),\dot x(t))$ for all $i$ and all
   $t\in[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]$.
2. **Uniqueness.** If $x:J\to Q$ and $\tilde x:\tilde J\to Q$ are motions of
   the model with the same initial datum,
   $x(t_{0})=\tilde x(t_{0})=x_{0}$ and $\dot x(t_{0})=\dot{\tilde x}(t_{0})=v_{0}$,
   then $x=\tilde x$ on $J\cap\tilde J$.
3. **Quantitative cylinder.** Let $h,r>0$ satisfy
   $C:=[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]\times\overline B(z_{0},r)\subseteq D$, put
   $M:=\sup\{\lVert\mathcal F(t,z)\rVert_{2}:(t,z)\in C\}$ and let $\Lambda$
   be a state-Lipschitz constant of $\mathcal F$ on $C$. If $hM\le r$ and
   $\Lambda h<1$, then there is exactly one motion on $[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]$
   through the datum whose state graph $(t,(x(t),\dot x(t)))$ lies in $C$, and
   every motion through the datum agrees with it on the intersection of its
   interval with $[t_{0}-h,t_{0}+h]$.
4. **Maximal motion.** There is exactly one maximal motion with the datum:
   its maximal interval $J_{\max}$ is an open interval containing $t_{0}$ and
   contained in $I_{0}$, and every motion with the datum is its restriction.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force model: clause 1 locates a
solution only near $t_{0}$ and bounds no interval length in terms of the data,
clause 4 asserts no completeness of $J_{\max}$ in $I_{0}$, and no empirical
content is claimed.

pthm-cm02-continuation.physical_scope: The continuation and breakdown criterion for the adopted Newtonian force model: the maximal motion of an initial datum is unique; at a finite right endpoint of its maximal interval its state graph leaves every compact subset of the open state domain, so a finite-time breakdown is caused by escape of the state (unbounded positions or velocities, or positions approaching the excluded configurations of the domain) or by the declared end of a finite time window; an autonomous force whose state is trapped in a compact subset of the state domain extends past the putative endpoint. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted force postulate and the cited mathematical continuation theorems; it asserts no global existence for particular force laws, no empirical statement and no claim that any physical system realizes the model.

pthm-cm02-continuation:
## Statement

Adopt the force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with time window
$I_{0}$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$, masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ and force map $F$ continuous and locally Lipschitz in the
state variable, locally uniformly in time; let $D=I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb
R^{3})^{N}$, $\mathcal F(t,x,v)=\bigl(v,\mathsf M^{-1}F(t,x,v)\bigr)$,
$U:=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$, and let motions, maximal motions and the state
curve $z=(x,\dot x)$ be as in [[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]. Fix an initial datum
$(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})\in I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$, write
$z_{0}=(x_{0},v_{0})$, and let $x_{\max}:J_{\max}\to Q$ be the maximal motion
with this datum, with state curve $z=(x_{\max},\dot x_{\max}):J_{\max}\to U$
and $J_{\max}=(a,b)$ its maximal interval, $-\infty\le a<b\le+\infty$.

1. **Existence and uniqueness of the maximal motion.** $J_{\max}$ is an open
   interval containing $t_{0}$ and contained in $I_{0}$, and every motion with
   the datum is a restriction of $x_{\max}$.
2. **Breakdown criterion.** If $b<+\infty$, then for every compact
   $K\subseteq D$ and every $\eta>0$ with $(b-\eta,b)\cap J_{\max}\neq\varnothing$
   there is $t\in(b-\eta,b)\cap J_{\max}$ with $(t,z(t))\notin K$. Equivalently:
   if there are a compact $K\subseteq D$ and $\delta>0$ with
   $(t,z(t))\in K$ for all $t\in(b-\delta,b)\cap J_{\max}$, then
   $x_{\max}$ extends to a motion of the model on a strictly larger interval
   than $J_{\max}$ — so $J_{\max}$ cannot have right endpoint $b$.
3. **Autonomous case.** Suppose $F$ does not depend on its time argument:
   $F(t,x,v)=F_{0}(x,v)$ for a map $F_{0}:U\to(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$ satisfying
   the standing regularity of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause (iii).
   Then the associated field is autonomous,
   $\mathcal F(t,x,v)=(v,\mathsf M^{-1}F_{0}(x,v))$, the equations do not use
   the time coordinate, and **the model is read on the extended time window
   $\mathbb R$** (the standing hypotheses are unchanged by the extension).
   With this reading, if there are a compact $K_{0}\subseteq U$ and
   $\delta>0$ with $z(t)\in K_{0}$ for all $t\in(b-\delta,b)\cap J_{\max}$,
   then $x_{\max}$ extends past $b$; consequently $b=+\infty$, and the motion
   is defined for all forward times $t\ge t_{0}$.
4. **Reading.** Suppose the time window is all of $\mathbb R$ (the
   time-dependent case included) and $b<+\infty$. Then for every compact
   $K_{0}\subseteq U$ and every $\delta>0$ there is $t\in(b-\delta,b)$ with
   $z(t)\notin K_{0}$: near a finite breakdown the state leaves every compact
   subset of the open state domain $U=Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$. Consequently a
   finite-time breakdown is caused either by unboundedness of the state or by
   approach of the positions to the complement of $Q$ (the configurations
   excluded from the model); the mere finiteness of $F$ at every point of $Q$
   prevents neither.

ex-cm02-uniform-field.physical_scope: A worked verification inside the framework: for one labeled particle of the model, the force map that assigns to every state the same vector $m\mathbf g$ (a declared constant field parameter of dimension length per time squared) satisfies the standing hypotheses of the force postulate; the explicit quadratic motion solves the initial-value problem, exists on the whole time window, is the unique maximal motion, and the model is covariant under changes of inertial frame with the parameter transforming as a spatial vector. The item is a computation inside the model: it asserts no measured value of any field strength, no property of the Earth's gravitational field and no empirical law, and the constant-field idealization is recorded as an approximation.

post-cm02-drag.physical_scope: Adoption of a constitutive force model for the interaction of a labeled particle with a medium: a linear drag force $-c\dot x$ with a declared coefficient $c\ge0$, optionally combined with a constant applied force. The model is phenomenological and restricted: it is adopted for a stated regime (slow motion in a viscous medium, the range in which the linear/Stokes form is used), its coefficient is a model parameter depending on body and medium, and the model neglects the random component of the environment's force. The item asserts no measured value, no derivation of the coefficient from the equation of motion, and no claim that the model applies to a given real motion.

post-cm02-drag:
## Postulate

**(i) Setting.** Work in the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with one labeled particle of fixed mass
$m>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)) in a fixed inertial frame, with
time window $\mathbb R$ and configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$, and with
the particle's coordinate position $x$ and coordinate velocity
$v=\dot x$ ([[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]]). The particle moves through a
**medium** that fills the region of the motion and is at rest in the chosen
frame. The medium is not one of the model's particle labels, so its effect on
the label is an **external force** of the model in the sense of clause (i) of
[[post-cm02-interactions]]: the decomposition into the label's own dynamics
and the medium's effect is part of the model's declaration.

**(ii) The model.** Adopt as a **constitutive model** of the medium's net
force the **linear drag model** with a declared coefficient
$c\ge0$ of dimension $\mu\tau^{-1}$, read in kilograms per second
([[def-cm01-units]]):

$$F^{\mathrm{drag}}(v):=-c\,v,$$

optionally combined, through the additive composition of clause (v) of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]], with a declared constant applied force
$m\mathbf g$, where $\mathbf g\in\mathbb R^{3}$ is a constant parameter of
dimension $\ell\tau^{-2}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]). The resulting force map of the
model is

$$F(t,x,v)=m\mathbf g-c\,v,\qquad\text{that is,}\qquad m\,\ddot x=m\mathbf g-c\,\dot x,$$

the equation of a label whose only interactions are the constant applied field
and the linear resistance of the medium. The model is defined for all
$(t,x,v)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3}\times\mathbb R^{3}$.

**(iii) Regularity.** The force map is affine in the state: it is continuous;
and for two states $z=(x,v)$, $z'=(x,v')$ sharing a position,
$\lVert F(t,z)-F(t,z')\rVert_{2}=c\,\lVert v-v'\rVert_{2}\le c\,\lVert z-z'\rVert_{2}$,
so it is locally Lipschitz in the state variable with the global constant $c$,
uniformly in time ([[def-locally-lipschitz-in-the-state-variable]]). It is
therefore a force map of the branch [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause
(iii), and the existence, uniqueness and continuation theorems of this page
apply to it; the regularity check is recorded with the model checks on the
companion page.

**(iv) Physical status and regime.** This is a **phenomenological**
constitutive model, adopted rather than derived: it represents the net effect
of a medium whose microscopic state is not modelled, and the coefficient $c$
is a model parameter that depends on the body and the medium. The linear form
is a restricted regime — slow motion through a viscous medium, of which the
Stokes force on a sphere, $c=6\pi\eta a$ for dynamic viscosity $\eta$ and
radius $a$, is the recorded example — and other regimes are **different
models**: a force growing quadratically in the speed at higher speeds, or
Coulomb sliding friction, whose expression contains the factor
$v/\lvert v\rvert$ and is undefined at $v=0$, and which is outside clause
(iii) of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] altogether. The model also neglects
the random component of the environment's force; the recorded source states
that this neglect is admissible only in a stated energy regime, in which the
system's energy scale greatly exceeds that of the environment's fluctuations.
No value of $c$, of $m$, or of $\mathbf g$ is asserted by this item, and using
measured values for them is an empirical premise with its own conditions and
uncertainty.

**(v) Status.** Adopted assumption of the framework when a model invokes it;
it selects no law of nature on its own and proves nothing about the actual
motion of any body in any medium. Its consequences within the model are the
subject of the companion example on terminal-velocity approach.

rem-cm02-open-system-warning.physical_scope: A scope and status audit of the force page: which objects are adopted model data, which statements are conditional deductions, which computations are examples, and which claims are deliberately not made; the boundary between the declared particle labels and their environment in an open-system description; the frame-selection content of external fields and apparatus; the empirical status of force-law parameters, drag regimes and model comparisons. Bookkeeping and scope only; it asserts no law, no measurement and no claim about nature beyond the items it cites.

ex-cm02-force-model-regularity-checks.physical_scope: A worked model check inside the framework: verification that three force maps of this page satisfy the standing continuity and state-local-Lipschitz hypotheses of the force postulate, with explicit constants where available; the uniform-force model has constant 0, the linear drag model has constant c, and the inverse-square external model is locally Lipschitz on each collision-free annulus with the stated constant and has no continuous extension to the excluded center. The item is a finite verification inside the adopted models; it asserts no motion, no measurement and no empirical claim.

ex-cm02-constant-field-projectile.physical_scope: A worked computation inside the constant-field model of [[ex-cm02-uniform-field]]: for a stated initial position, speed and launch angle and a declared constant field parameter, the trajectory is planar and parabolic, the return-to-launch-height time and the level range are computed from the model, and the motion is the unique maximal motion through the datum. The item asserts no measured value of any field strength or launch parameter, models no medium and no drag, and records that the constant-field description of a realistic field is an approximation.

ex-cm02-drag-terminal-velocity.physical_scope: A worked computation inside the linear drag model of [[post-cm02-drag]] with a constant applied force: for a stated initial position and velocity the explicit motion is verified, it is the unique maximal motion and exists for all real times, and its velocity converges to the terminal velocity $(m/c)\mathbf g$ with an explicit exponential bound. The item is a conditional computation inside the model; the coefficient and field parameters are declared model data, no measured value is asserted, and the phenomenological and regime qualifications of the drag postulate are preserved.

cex-cm02-nonunique-flow-for-a-continuous.physical_scope: A refutation, inside the framework's equation of motion, of the claim that a merely continuous force map suffices for uniqueness of the motion through an initial datum: the unit-mass model in three dimensions with force $F(x)=m\sqrt{|x_1|}e_1$ is continuous but not state-locally-Lipschitz at the origin, and exhibits two distinct $C^2$ motions through the rest datum. The item refutes only the weakened variant of the force postulate in which continuity replaces the local-Lipschitz clause; it asserts no motion of any physical body, no measurement and no empirical claim.

cex-cm02-singular-collision-finite-time.physical_scope: A refutation, inside the model, of the claim that every motion of the inverse-square external-potential model exists for all real times: for one label of mass $m>0$ in the external potential $U(x)=-k/|x|$ on the collision-excluded domain, an explicit radial motion with the stated initial data solves the model on $(-\infty,T)$ and has no extension past the finite time $T$, at which the position reaches the excluded center and the speed is unbounded. The item refutes only the all-time-existence claim for this model, illustrates the escape alternative of the breakdown criterion, and asserts no motion of any physical body, no measurement and no empirical claim.
